critic.verdict:
film: The pull-back works — it opens tight on the boy's small silhouette at t=0 and, over the six frames, visibly widens to reveal the full lantern-lit shophouse street, with the boy shrinking into the scene and settling at scale 0.94. That reads as an arrival/reveal for 'Arrival in Chinatown' and is clearly better than a plain centred push-in. The boy stays a coherent solid silhouette throughout (no tearing, doubled edges, halo or painted-over ghost at his original spot), his bundle stays with him, and no layer clips the frame edge awkwardly beyond the intentional initial camera crop. First frame is a legible tight opening picture; last frame (t=1, zoom 1) is a balanced wide street view good to dwell on while reading. Light-sweep is subtle and fits dusk lanterns; the sepia copperplate/cross-hatch print style is preserved.  
plate: No stray text, letters or numbers; the boy is correctly a silhouette from behind with a cloth bundle and no drawn face; rickshaws, paper lanterns and shophouses are period-correct for 1930s Singapore; no broken anatomy or melted objects visible.
